MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MONDAY, DECEMBER 2, 2024

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order by CHAIR MEDAWAR at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Medawar, Nicklas, Olson, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli,
  Schachter, Yoo

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner
  Katrina Kawagoe, Assistant Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, NOVEMBER 4, 2024

VICE CHAIR OLSON, made a motion seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE THE CORRECTED PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES OF
  NOVEMBER 4, 2024.

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READY BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240198; ADDRESS: 31 CLEAR VISTA DRIVE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: CURT DITTMAN, C DITTMAN
  DESIGN; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (ND-
  240204) and approval of a Grading application (G-240197) for the construction of retaining
  walls, including one replacement wall, with a maximum depth of fill of five feet, all at the
  rear of the property.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. PA-240428. The proposal includes removal of the existing retaining wall, which is
failing, and removal of the existing exterior staircase and landing. It will be replaced by a 5 FT.
and 2.5 FT. retaining wall and associated grading. The staircase will be replaced, and a new 167
SF patio will be constructed between the two walls, which will act as a landing for the stairs.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 2, 2024
  1
 Senior Planner stated that the project conforms to the Neighborhood Compatibility ordinance and
the meets the five criteria for approval of a Grading Permit.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve PA-
240198, subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report.

VICE CHAIR OLSON requested clarification on the tennis court’s 5 FT. retaining wall and exterior
staircase that was approved in 1984 and asked if the approval was for a wooden retaining wall.
Senior Planner Berry stated that portions of the wall are wood; however, there are no copies of
the drawings for the wall.

VICE CHAIR OLSON stated that there is a 5 FT. retaining wall in the lower part of the property
and asked if it is not being replaced nor failing. Senior Planner Berry stated that the lower retaining
wall is not being replaced or addressed as part of this project.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if staff received comments from 29 or 33 Clear Vista. Senior
Planner stated that no comments were received from any neighbors.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI inquired about the adjacent neighbor’s portion of the wall and if
there is any need for improvement. Senior Planner Berry stated that she would like to defer the
question to the project applicant.

Curt Dittman, Designer/Property Owner Representative, stated that the homeowner requested
the design, and they have not been in communication with the adjacent neighbor about continuing
the replacement of the wall. He stated that he did not see significant distress of the wall and stated
that this is a preventive measure, and that the replacement of the stairs is for better access since
the existing stairs are very steep.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS asked if there would be a tie-in to the adjacent wall. Mr. Dittman
stated that there will be a cutoff with a return to the new wall, creating a box.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Mr. Dittman stated that retaining
walls are designed in 1 FT. segments and do not rely on the adjoining wall segment. Additionally,
he stated that a soils report is not needed since the wall is being replaced and there will be no
grading, only compaction behind the new wall.

Director Naughton stated that a building permit will be required for this project and the building
and safety team will determine if a soils report will be required.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240198 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITIONS
  OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, REPP-LOADSMAN, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER, YOO
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-240198, a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination and approval of a Grading Application
for 31 Clear Vista Drive. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or
the City Council by its own motion may appeal this project.

  B. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240465; ADDRESS: 27 AURORA DRIVE, ROLLING
  HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: CRISS GUNDERSON, AIA; DESCRIPTION:
  A request for approval of a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-240466) for
  442 square feet of single-story additions to an existing single-story residence and two
  Minor Deviations to construct an addition that will reduce the existing front yard by less
  than 10% (MD-240467) and encroach into an existing front yard, not projecting beyond
  the forwardmost building line (MD-240468)

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. PA-240465. The applicant proposes to construct three small additions, one of
which will encroach into the front yard and two within the rear yard. The garage addition will extend
5 FT into the front yard and add 102 SF to the garage. The back wall of the garage will be
demolished and the wall will be moved forward by approximately 5 FT. Additionally, there will be
a 144 SF addition to the rear of the home to accommodate a new bedroom and bathroom, and a

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 2, 2024
  2
 196 SF addition for a new office and two expand a bedroom and playroom. Lastly, in order to
create a consistent plate height, the applicant proposes to raise the ridge height from 15’-9” to
16’-6”.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that the project meets the requirements for Neighborhood
Compatibility. There are two Minor Deviations required, and the project conforms with the
ordinance and does not conflict with any other provisions of the zoning code.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-240465, subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report.

Criss Gunderson, Architect stated that he is available to answer any questions.

There were no questions for Mr. Gunderson.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR OLSON to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICAITION NO. PA-240465  SUBJECT  TO  THE
  CONDITIONS OUTLINED IN THE STAFF REPORT.

AYES: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, REPP-LOADSMAN, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER, YOO
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning Application No.
PA-240465, a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination and two Minor Deviations at 27 Aurora
Drive. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or the City Council by
its own motion may appeal the project.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240444; ADDRESS: 26444 CRENSHAW BLVD,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: KAREN SHIPHERD, ROLLING
  HILLS COUNTRY DAY SCHOOL; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Conditional Use Permit
  (CUP-240438) for the continued operation of a kindergarten through eighth grade private
  day school and the construction of a new 828 square foot library and 228 square foot
  administrative office addition.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. PA-240444. An overview of previous CUP’s approved for the property was
provided. Parking requirements and exterior noise considerations were evaluated as part of this
CUP review. The proposed project complies with the required CUP findings for approval.

Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open
the public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt
Resolution No. PA-240444, approving the project.

VICE CHAIR OLSON asked about the reciprocal parking agreements with the South Coast
Botanical Gardens and Rolling Hills United Methodist Church and what would occur if either party
terminated the parking agreement. Assistant Planner Kawagoe stated that the parking
agreements are a condition of approval; the City would be alerted and Rolling Hills Country Day
School would need to find alternatives to be in compliance with the City’s parking standards.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

There were no questions of comments.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

VICE CHAIR OLSON made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER NICKLAS to,

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 2, 2024
  3
   ADOPT PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240444.

Ayes: MEDAWAR, OLSON, NICKLAS, REPP-LOADSMAN, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER, YOO
Noes:
Absent:
Abstain:

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. PA-240444
for a Conditional Use Permit for the continued operation of a kindergarten through eighth grade
private day school and the construction of a new 828 square foot library and 228 square foot
administrative office. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public or the
City Council by its own motion may appeal this project.

B.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240484; ADDRESS: 13 DAPPLEGRAY LANE,
  ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: ADRIAN CRACIUN, ABOVE
  DESIGN, INC.; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Variance (V-240485) to allow an 80-
  square-foot enlargement to a back porch with a nonconforming setback from the rear of
  property line.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. PA-240484. The project proposed to expand an existing rear porch by 80 SF and
add additional exterior stairs to allow for improved access from the residence to the backyard,
specifically for a newly proposed pool.

Senior Planner Berry stated the property was built in 1957, which is the same year that the City
was incorporated. The property was developed according to Los Angeles County’s development
standards. A Variance is required to enlarge the existing nonconforming rear porch. The proposed
conforms with the Variance findings. The applicants have discussed the project with their
neighbors and the Dapplegray Lanes Property Owners Association (DLPOA) and there were no
concerns or issues with this project.

Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public
hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt Resolution
No. PA-240484, approving the project.

VICE CHAIR OLSON stated that there was a zone clearance for a pool approved in 2015 and the
pool was not built; and asked if the zone clearance remains valid. Senior Planner Berry stated
that if a building permit is not pulled within six months of approval, the zone clearance is null and
void.

COMMISSIONER NICKLAS inquired about the pool and why it is not part of the planning
application being considered. Senior Planner Berry stated that pools are administrative approvals
as long as the required setbacks are met. The setback for a pool is 5 FT.

VICE CHAIR OLSON recused himself from discussion and voting since he knows the property
owner.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR inquired about any requirements around the pool for safety.
Director Naughton stated that the building code requirements can be met with fencing or alarms
on all doors/windows leading to the pool area.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if there is a reason that the easement running
through the property has not been vacated. Senior Planner Berry stated that it is her
understanding that this is an easement that was granted to the DLPOA and not a city access
easement.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if there was any support of objection from the neighbors. Senior
Planner Berry stated that there were no written comments; however, the property owner reached
out to the neighbors, and they were in support of the project. The neighbors also received a public
hearing notice for this project.

COMMISSIONER YOO made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 2, 2024
  4
 Mr. Craciun, Project Designer, stated that he is available for any questions.
There were no questions or comments for Mr. Craciun.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-
LOADSMAN to,

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER REPP-
LOADSMAN to,

  ADOPT PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240484.

Ayes: MEDAWAR, NICKLAS, REPP-LOADSMAN, ROMANELLI, SCHACHTER, YOO
Noes:
Absent:
Abstain: OLSON

Director Naughton stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. PA-240484
a Resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates granting a Variance
to allow a 80 SF enlargement to a back porch with a nonconforming setback from the rear property
line at 13 Dapplegray Lane. There is a 20-day appeal period by which any member of the public
or the City Council by its own motion may appeal this project.

C.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-240141; ADDRESS: 758 SILVER SPUR ROAD
  (BART EARL WAY), ROLLING HILLS ESTATES, CA 90274; APPLICANT: MOSTAFA
  RAHIMI; DESCRIPTION:A request for a Conditional Use Permit (CUP-240140) to operate
  a medical office use, a Precise Plan of Design (PPD-240142) for exterior improvements
  to an existing commercial building and a Variance (V-240478) to allow the site to maintain
  less than twenty percent of the existing surface parking area as landscaped area.

For the record, CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that his business is located near the subject property;
however, he does not know the applicant.

Senior Planner Berry provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning
Application No. 240141. The building was constructed in 1970 and was previously occupied by a
KFC fast food restaurant from the early 1970’s to the early 2000’s and in 2009, the building was
occupied by a dry-cleaning business with off-site laundering operations. The property has nine
parking spaces in the rear and two entrances from Bart Earle Way. The total landscaping is
approximately 500 SF or 5% of the overall site, per the Municipal Code the required landscaping
is 20% with 10% being in the parking lot areas; this property is considered non-conforming.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the applicant is proposing a medical office use, which requires a
CUP in the CGMU district. The applicant made improvements to the exterior of the property
without permits and requires approval of a Precise Plan of Design. The applicant requests a
Variance to incrementally reduce and maintain the nonconforming landscape at the site.

Senior Planner Berry stated that this office will provide concierge medical services to geriatric
patients who are referred by sister facilities owned by the same doctor (applicant). The office will
have two staff, the doctor and receptionist, and there will be up to four patients per day.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the findings for a Conditional Use permit can be made. The
Precise Plan of Design meets the criteria for approval. The work conducted without permits has
been conditioned as part of this application and the applicant is required to obtain after-the-fact
permits prior to occupancy. Senior Planner Berry provided a detailed list of items, known to staff,
that have been improved without the benefit of permits.

Senior Planner Berry stated that two letters were received and emailed to the Planning
Commission prior to the meeting. One was a letter of support for the project and the other was a
letter from the applicant stating that an oxygen tank currently being stored at the site will be
removed.

Senior Planner Berry stated that the project was reviewed in accordance with the California
Environmental Quality Act and was determined to be exempt under Class 1, existing facilities.

 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 2, 2024
  5
 Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission open the public
hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing; and adopt Resolution
No. PA-240141, approving the project.

CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if staff has looked at the narrow exit driveway and asked if the applicant
has proposed improvements to secure patients who will be exiting the driveway. Senior Planner
Berry stated that the plans were sent to the City’s Traffic Engineer and discussed the existing
drive aisles and driveways and understand that the conditions are not ideal. In respect to the drive
aisle the requirement is 8 FT and the exit aisle for this site is 8.5 FT. At this time, there is no
proposed signage; however, this can be added as a condition of approval.

CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if there is consideration to have patients enter through the rear of the
building. Senior Planner Berry stated that the reception area is in the front of the building;
however, the plans show an existing door and entrance area in the rear.

In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Director Naughton stated that the
City’s Code Compliance Officer drove by and noticed work being done at the site; there were no
permits for the work and a stop work notice was issued. The stop work notice was violated multiple
times and work continued on the exterior and interior of the building. Staff has not been granted
access for an interior inspection and from what staff can tell, non-loadbearing walls were added
and there was some electrical. The exterior work is cosmetic improvements.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about the retaining wall that has been an issue. Director
Naughton recommends that a condition of approval be added for the applicant to provide an
assessment of the wall by a qualified professional within a specific time frame.

CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that the retaining wall along the rear of the buildings on Bart Earle Way
is on Rancho Palos Verdes property and it is a good idea to require an assessment as a condition
of approval.

CHAIR MEDAWAR inquired about the environmental report provided and expressed his concern
about making sure there are no contaminants in the soil from the previous dry-cleaning business.
Senior Planner Naughton stated that the report is part of Phase I of the environmental
assessment. There are two additional phases.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN inquired if the California Regional Water Control Board
was involved in with this property. Senior Planner Berry stated that typically staff will take a look
at lists that are compiled by the State and other local agencies; there were no records for this site.

VICE CHAIR OLSON asked if there are any other mansard roofs in the commercial district. Senior
Planner Berry stated that there are not.

COMMISSIONER YOO asked if the number of patients increased from the four patients would
